title: The twelve sent out (Luke 9:1–17)
hookLine: sent with nothing, then the five thousand fed
carry: you give them something to eat

lines: NO STAFF, NO BAG, NO BREAD, NO MONEY.
cards: No walking stick, no bag, no bread, no money, no spare clothes. That's the packing list Jesus gives the twelve.
In the King James words: "Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece." A scrip is a traveler's bag.
They go out empty-handed, village by village, to preach and to heal, depending on whoever opens a door. Until now they've watched; now they're sent.
And word spreads so far that Herod himself, who had John beheaded, hears and is perplexed. Who is this? He wants to see him.

teach.b: The twelve come back full of stories, and Jesus takes them aside privately, to a deserted place near a town called Bethsaida. The crowds follow.
Luke says Jesus "received them," spoke about the kingdom, and healed those who needed it. The sun gets low.

And the twelve, sensibly, say: "Send the multitude away, that they may go into the towns and country round about, and lodge, and get victuals: for we are here in a desert place." It's a reasonable plan.
Jesus answers, short and plain: "Give ye them to eat." You feed them. They've just come back from a journey where they carried nothing; now he hands the problem back to them.
They count: "We have no more but five loaves and two fishes." About five thousand men, Luke says. Jesus has them sit in groups of about fifty, like guests at a meal.
He takes the loaves and fish, looks up to heaven, blesses, breaks, and gives to the disciples to set before the crowd.
Later, at the Last Supper, nearly the same movements return: took, gave thanks, broke, gave. Everyone eats and is filled, and they pick up twelve baskets of leftovers.
Some readers notice: one for each of the twelve who said send them away. Jesus didn't do it without them. He did it through their hands, with what they already had, which was almost nothing.

how: Some Christian food pantries and church meal programs take "give ye them to eat" as a motto, and Christians often notice in this meal the actions of the Last Supper and communion: taking, blessing, breaking and giving bread.

games.q: you're one of the twelve. it's late, you're in a deserted place, and there are thousands of hungry people. what do you suggest?
o: send them away to find food and lodging.
ask what we have and bring it to Jesus.
games.why: the disciples said send them away. Jesus answered: give ye them to eat. and their five loaves and two fish fed everyone.

practice: Think of one small comfort you could set aside for a day, the second coffee, the show, the scrolling before sleep, not as punishment but to notice how much you usually carry.

Then picture what that small saving of money or time could become in someone else's hands: a meal, a gift, an hour. If you pray, you can offer that small thing to God; if you don't, simply decide where it goes.

wordCard.voice: Scrip, an old word for a traveler's bag: Jesus sends the twelve out with nothing, then hands them a hungry crowd and five loaves, and through their hands five thousand are fed.

orig.note: Greek: you give them to eat. the "you" is emphatic.

carryVoice: Your line: you give them something to eat. Almost nothing, in their hands, fed a crowd. Day five hundred thirty-four.
